question: True or false: a 230-decibel click underwater carries the same intensity as a 230-decibel sound in air?
answer: False. Underwater decibels are measured against 1 micropascal, air decibels against 20, a 26 dB gap; and because water is so much denser and stiffer, equal intensity needs about 36 dB more pressure. Subtract roughly 62 dB to compare. A sperm whale's click, near 230 dB in water, is immensely loud, but on another scale.
move: A decibel is a ratio; ask what it is a ratio to.
ask: Which number do I quote without asking what it is a ratio to?
trap: Reading a decibel figure as one absolute scale, whatever the medium.
source: Au & Hastings, Principles of Marine Bioacoustics, 2008
reference: Au & Hastings, Principles of Marine Bioacoustics, Springer, 2008; Møhl et al., The monopulsed nature of sperm whale clicks, Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 2003
